headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the filesystem and execute code, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways with Khoj’s shared indexed notes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and Open Interpreter can read the filesystem and use clipboard/stdin-stdout, so attacker-controlled content in shared files can flow from agent_a into agent_b as instructions. This is not a pure manual copy-paste path; the shared filesystem and permissive parsing make injection plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes a file containing adversarial instructions and Open Interpreter later reads that file as task context, injection is possible.
IF the operator uses shared notes or copied outputs as prompts between the agents, the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories with no shared notes.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files into Khoj indexes.
Require manual review of any file before Open Interpreter reads it.
Use a dedicated prompt prefix that strips instructions from retrieved text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging so Open Interpreter ignores retrieved instructions from Khoj.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress. In default configurations, sensitive content indexed by agent_a can be exposed to agent_b and then transmitted outward by agent_b without a built-in isolation boundary.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same user account and share local files, agent_b can access data indexed by agent_a.
IF Open Interpreter sends retrieved file contents to its model provider or external APIs, those contents can leave the machine.
mitigations: Run each agent under a separate OS user.
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory.
Exclude personal notes from Khoj indexing unless explicitly approved.
Block outbound network access for Open Interpreter during sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read the filesystem, and Open Interpreter can write files and modify git state while Khoj maintains shared index state across clients. That creates a direct write-conflict pathway on shared resources, with Open Interpreter able to overwrite or mutate files that Khoj indexes or serves.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory tree, file-level races and overwrites can occur.
IF Open Interpreter edits git-tracked files while Khoj indexes them concurrently, stale or conflicting state can be served.
mitigations: Give each agent a separate workspace.
Pause Khoj indexing while Open Interpreter performs writes.
Avoid letting Open Interpreter touch git repositories used by Khoj.
Use filesystem snapshots before agent_b writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared index and workspace mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from indexed documents, and Open Interpreter can act on those outputs with code execution and filesystem writes. If agent_b treats agent_a’s retrieved text as authoritative, a mistaken or poisoned retrieval can cascade into destructive actions or incorrect commits.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter uses Khoj output as the basis for shell commands or file edits without verification, errors can cascade.
IF Khoj retrieves stale or adversarial notes and Open Interpreter executes them, downstream harm can be amplified.
mitigations: Require a human approval step before any Open Interpreter action.
Cross-check Khoj outputs against source files before acting.
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only mode for retrieval-derived tasks.
Use short-lived scratch files for intermediate outputs.
requires-engineering: add structured verification between retrieval and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj is oriented around personal notes and indexed documents, while Open Interpreter can access the entire local machine and broad network egress. That combination can create compliance mismatches for retention, residency, or subject-rights handling, but the profiles do not specify a concrete regulated data class like PHI or EU-only data.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj indexes and Open Interpreter processes the same files, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the operator relies on different deletion or export workflows for each agent, subject-rights handling can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Document which data classes each agent may touch.
Keep regulated data out of shared local files.
Align retention settings before use.
Review outbound destinations for Open Interpreter.
requires-engineering: implement unified deletion/export workflows.
